description.purpose: An interactive canvas of the colony, reached at /<mount>/ on the colony's one listener. A mutation receipt takes a topology snapshot, a code cell turns it into display objects, and a `web` cell holds them and serves the page. The browser owns the drag and the camera; nothing else. Since 2.2.0 the refresh cadence is a LITERAL inside `./clock`'s `params.schedules` rather than a `CANVY_REFRESH_CRON` substitution token out of the colony's environment ([#138](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/138), ruling R-0904-6), so two canvases in one colony refresh at different cadences -- the environment form had one value for all of them. Since 2.3.2 the display refs `web@2.1.0`, whose socket carries a second kind of foreign topic ([#766](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/766)) on top of the patch bundle of 2.0.4 ([#718](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/718)) and its one frame per route ([#723](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/723)). Only the ref pin moves -- no cell, no lane and no declaration of this hive -- which is why it is the third place (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Since 2.3.3 the display refs `web@2.2.0`, whose page shell carries no inline script ([#867](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/867)). The canvas itself still writes an inline client script whose hash nobody publishes, so a canvas does not run under `script-src 'self'` yet. Only the ref pin moves -- no cell, no lane and no declaration of this hive -- which is why it is the third place (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Since 2.3.4 the display refs `web@2.3.0` ([#1001](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/1001)). Only the ref pin moves -- no cell, no lane and no declaration of this hive -- which is why it is the third place (`docs/development-rules.md` § 4/4a). Since 2.4.0 there is no timer in here (R-AG-1, GH #1096): the hive accepts `mutation_committed` -- the receipt the mutation door leaves when the graph moved (GH #553) -- and its own door turns it into `in_refresh`, the pattern `colony-view` took in 1.1.0. The minute tick over an unchanged graph is gone, and so is the `clock` cell; a removed interior cell and a new lane are the second digit (docs/development-rules.md § 4/4a).
description.use_when: Somebody should see and rearrange something the colony knows, in a browser. One canvy per canvas: two canvases are two hives under two mounts, which is what makes one reverse-proxy rule a complete access statement for one of them.
description.not_in_scope: It draws nothing the topology snapshot does not hold, and that snapshot is taken on a mutation receipt through this hive's OWN lane to the colony's read-only graph endpoint (GH #163), so the canvas is as fresh as the graph. No authentication and no TLS: since `canvy@2.3.0` the display owns no port at all -- it hangs on the colony's one listener under `override_params.web.mount` -- and whatever stands in front of that listener is somebody else's job (R-W8-2). No object library beyond cells, hives and edges. No interior address: `params.ports` is empty, so no cell in here is an endpoint -- a caller names the hive and a lane (in_refresh in, event out).
examples: GET http://127.0.0.1:7777/canvy/ -- the colony, draggable, arrangement persistent (7777 is the colony's own listener, /canvy/ the mount this template ships)
a drag -> object:set on the node's x and y -> a diff to every open browser, without one message entering the colony
every minute: a topology snapshot -> one bundle of object calls -> the picture catches up
